title: Science that had Developed Then
paragraphs: Tolkāppiyam embodies, both suggestively and explicitly, qualities and characteristics of things, modes of living of the ancient days and basic structures of phenomena which are relevant to the present time. Even though some of them may not bear on modern customs and the new world thinking, they, nevertheless, remain valuable treasure troves of history left by the ancient Tamils. The following verse represents the acme of ancient Tamils’ scientific knowledge base:

> Single-sense organisms have the sense of touch; > Two-sense organisms are endowed with touch and taste; > Touch, taste and smell go with three-sense organisms; > Four-sense organisms have sight added to the three; > Five-sense organisms are gifted with hearing in addition; > Mind’s faculty is the sixth sense known, > Thus goes the classification by discerning men.

That is, beings with one sense feel through the body. Two-sense beings use body and mouth. Three-sense beings have the faculties of body, mouth and nose. Four-sense beings employ body, mouth, nose and eye. Five-sense beings enjoy the
faculties of body, mouth, nose, eye and ear. Six-sense beings have the gift of mind in addition to the five above. Thus all living things on the earth have been classified into six categories.

This classification apart, Tolkāppiyar identifies the beings that are endowed with each of these six classes of faculties. That the ancient Tamils have written the grammar of life on the earth on scientific basis just amazes us.

The division of living things into six categories on the basis of the five senses and the sense organs has been done in terms of their hierarchy of intelligence and power - which demonstrates the scientific knowledge and scientific perception of phenomena of the ancient Tamils. This knowledge and perception constitute the core of the grammar of life propounded in Tolkāppiyam.
> The grass and tree are single-sense organisms; > Other species of the flora there are too > That are limited to this faculty.
> The snail and shell-fish are two-sense organisms; > Others of their species there are too.

These verses show that grass and tree are one-sense beings using the faculty of the body. Be it noted that Tolkāppiyar states that there are other species too that are one-sense organisms. Such of these instances show Tolkāppiyam to be a treasure-house of scientific knowledge and information.
Look at the following verses where Tolkāppiyam gives examples of the beings that are endowed with two, three, four and five faculties.

> The snail and shell-fish are two-sense organisms; > Others of their species there are too. > The termite and ant are three-sense organisms; > There are others of their kind confined to these faculties. > The crabs and beetles are four-sense organisms; > Others of their species there are too. > The beasts and men sans discrimination > Are creatures with five senses; > There are co-sharers among their species too.
Human beings have six senses. If some people are deficient in one or two of these or if they do not use them properly, Tolkāppiyam is in no way responsible for it.
